prompt.en: The Emergency (1975-77) showed both the vulnerabilities and the resilience of democratic institutions in India. Explain this statement, referring to what was imposed in June 1975, what happened during the Emergency, and how the period ended.

label.en: Gives the context: dissatisfaction over unemployment, inflation and allegations of misgovernance led to widespread protests, and a National Emergency was imposed in June 1975 on the grounds of internal disturbance

accepted: its safeguards and citizens restore it
voters can remove misuse of power

text.en: The years 1975 to 1977 were one of the major challenges to democracy in India, and they showed two things at once.
In June 1975, a National Emergency was imposed on the grounds of internal disturbance, after unemployment, inflation and allegations of misgovernance had led to widespread protests.

During the Emergency, a majority of Fundamental Rights were suspended, the press was censored, and numerous political leaders and activists were arrested. Democratic institutions came under severe strain.
The Emergency was lifted in 1977, general elections were held, and people expressed their will through the ballot. The ruling government was defeated.
The period highlighted the importance of constitutional safeguards, civil liberties and active citizen participation.
The Emergency therefore showed both the vulnerabilities and the resilience of democratic institutions: they can be harmed, and they can recover through safeguards and active citizens.
